title: 16 System Design Ideas That Keep Apps Alive
subtitle: From idempotent APIs to Bloom filters, the beginner map for 2026
intro: You saved Neo Kim's list of 16 system design concepts for 2026 — the same playbook 200K+ engineers get in his newsletter. Where do you even start?
takeaway: System design is choosing trade-offs so your app stays fast, correct, and available as it grows.

sections.heading: Analogy: a city, not a single building
sections.body: Think of your app like a city. One building is one server; a city is many buildings with roads. A distributed system is that city — many computers working together over a network to act like one app. Service discovery is the address book that helps them find each other.

sections.heading: Why it exists: speed, safety, and scale
sections.body: Why use these ideas? To stay fast and correct as more people join. An idempotent API means retrying the same request has the same effect as doing it once — tap pay twice, pay once. Consistent hashing is a way to spread users evenly across servers when you add more. A Bloom filter is a quick check for "have we seen this?" to skip slow lookups. JWT authentication is a signed pass that proves who you are.

sections.heading: What can go wrong: when the city jams
sections.body: What can go wrong? Coordination. The saga pattern breaks a big job into steps with undo actions — if an undo fails, data stays mismatched. RPC is when one service calls another directly; it can time out and, without idempotency, retries create duplicates. Bloom filters can also give false positives, saying "maybe yes" when the answer is no.

steps.narration: You tap pay twice; network may send it twice.
Idempotent API ensures second tap does not double-charge.
Service discovery finds which server can handle it.
Consistent hashing picks the right server evenly.
Bloom filter quickly checks if we've seen this payment.
JWT proves who you are without extra DB call.

quiz.q: What does an idempotent API guarantee?
options: Retrying the same request has the same effect as once
quiz.why: Idempotency means safe retries — duplicates don't create extra side effects like double charges.

quiz.q: What fails first if usage grows 100x without consistent hashing?
options: Adding servers reshuffles most users to new machines, causing hot spots and cache misses
Saga pattern is no longer needed
quiz.why: Without consistent hashing, scaling out remaps many keys, overloading new nodes and breaking locality.

quiz.q: What is a key limit of Bloom filters?
options: They can give false positives — saying maybe present when not
quiz.why: Bloom filters are fast probabilistic checks; they never miss a true present item but can falsely say maybe.

extra: Saga pattern is often used as alternative to two-phase commit for long-lived transactions across microservices.
